scenes.say: Here are five everyday foods your eyes love. Let's count down.

scenes.en: Guava, orange and amla are rich in vitamin C.
scenes.say: Number five. Fruits like guava, orange and amla. They are rich in vitamin C, which helps protect the eye's tissues.

scenes.en: Sardine and mackerel have omega-3 fats, good for the retina.
scenes.say: Number four. Oily fish like sardine and mackerel. Their healthy omega three fats are good for the retina.

scenes.en: The yolk has lutein, a yellow pigment your retina uses.
scenes.say: Number three. Eggs. The yolk has lutein and zeaxanthin, natural yellow pigments found in the centre of your retina.

scenes.en: Carrot, pumpkin and papaya: vitamin A helps you see in dim light.
scenes.say: Number two. Carrots, pumpkin and papaya. Their vitamin A helps your eyes see in dim light.

scenes.en: Keerai and spinach: one of the richest sources of eye pigments.
scenes.say: And number one. Leafy greens like spinach. They are one of the richest sources of lutein for your eyes.

scenes.en: Lack of vitamin A is a leading cause of preventable blindness in children (WHO).
scenes.ta: வைட்டமின் A குறைபாடு குழந்தைகளின் பார்வையைப் பாதிக்கும்
scenes.say: Did you know? The WHO says lack of vitamin A is a leading cause of preventable blindness in children. If a child struggles to see at dusk, see an eye specialist soon.

scenes.en: Food can't fix your power. Book an eye test.
scenes.ta: உணவு கண்ணாடிக்கு மாற்று அல்ல – பரிசோதனை அவசியம்
scenes.say: Good food supports your eyes, but it can't fix your power. Book an eye test today.
